title: Apparent calibration or data processing issue reported (with Libre/Blucon)
body:
I've been using xdrip for awhile and honestly after you continuously update it 
 by doing calibrations work with that it does a pretty good job eventually the readings received are very very close to what I get with the finger testing. the problem that I notice is that sometimes the app seems to be getting into a some kind of a dormant state specially when we are on the lower level today for example I felt very sick and kind of week like I was down in the 50s and I know because I've been a diabetic for very long time and then xdrip was just telling me that I was 77 so I decided to check with my libre sensor and it was reporting 53 then I used the same sensor but this time I did a blood test and it actually give me 33 and I tried to add the 53 to the calibrations of the app and it accepted it and adjusted itself a little bit but we're talking about 20 difference which on the lower side it's very dangerous but then when I tried to enter 33 as calibration and xdrip told me that it was impossible for me to enter because he was out of range. I'm sorry if I'm being bragging but that is a problem on the lower side, some times xdrip sticks to a level and does not moves from there. I would reallyy appreciate the author to step in. Thanks

... and this is done on purpose out of various reasons:

1) When you are low, you should eat something, not calibrate!
2) As a low value most likely comes from a drop (no one stays low constantly), it is not a good value to calibrate.
3) As you will eat some glucose, the value will soon rise again -> again not a stable value for calibration
4) On low values, the allowed error of a glucose meter of 15mg/dl (Europe) or 20mg/dl (US) would be quite a large percentage.

I'd suggest you calibrate on stable values that are low-normal and on stable values that are highish-normal and stable. You will need some distance between the calibrations (in BG value) as if they too close together they won't determine a distinctive linear curve.

And if you have a fingerstick of 33mg/dl (1.8mmol/l !!!) - please treat the low and don't play around with your tech.

I would have preferred your comments to be related to the tech part of my
question and not to fall in some kind of paternal sermon.

Being diabetic for over 20 years I know exactly what I'm supposed to do
when I have a low special in the 33 range. I didn't think that I was
supposed to write in this board that I had some sugar to take care of my
low levels.  my question was why the app does not move from where it is and
stays in the 70s when actually there is such a big difference with what the
actual values are. expecially considering the whole time readings are right
on.

I'm not here to argue so please refrain from debating my reply and let's
stick to useful troubleshooting info.. Thanks

In the standard configuration the glucose value is going to be related in a linear way to the raw sensor value received. If xDrip is showing a flat graph but blood glucose is dropping significantly it implies that the raw sensor value is not matching that.

With Libre temperature is also a factor which is significant but not yet included in the calibration algorithm. Could there be anything unusual with the temperature of the sensor occurring? I assume it is a european sensor and is being worn on the back of the arm.

The calibration graph shows that @jo1st is likely using the Datricsae calibration algorithm which I did write.

The main reason this issue doesn't have any real way to resolve it is that what is being reported doesn't make any sense, hasn't been reported before and may well be an issue out of our control. We certainly don't have any way to reproduce it.

As a mentioned before if the reported glucose value stays the same while blood sugar is actually significantly dropping then it implies that the raw data we are receiving from the sensor is staying the same. 

This is unlikely an algorithm issue and the calibration graph looks sensible and there are no indications from the screenshot of any systemic problem in data processing nor have we had that reported before.
